title: Book 6 — Erato, Chapter 117
paragraphs: In this battle at Marathon about six thousand four hundred of the barbarians were killed, and one hundred and ninety-two of the Athenians. Such was the tally of the dead on both sides. And there happened there a marvel of this kind: an Athenian named Epizelos son of Couphagoras, fighting in the close combat and acquitting himself bravely, was deprived of the sight of his eyes, though he had received no blow on any part of his body and had not been hit by any missile; from that moment to the end of his life he remained blind. I was told that the story he used to tell about what had befallen him was this: that it seemed to him a tall man in full armor stood against him, whose beard cast a shadow across his whole shield; that this apparition passed him by, but killed the man standing next to him. This is the tale Epizelos used to tell, as I was informed.
